headline: The A/B experiment could not be executed against the real resolver. Candidate 2 is therefore NOT proven and must not be implemented.

whatWasAttempted.approach: fetch chapter-app.js as text, append one export line before the final })(); so lookupWord/classesCompatible/wordClassOf become reachable, then serve that copy inline in place of the original <script src="chapter-app.js"> via srcdoc + <base href>. The production file on disk was never edited and the app still executes exactly once.
whatWasAttempted.whyThisApproach: the brief forbids reimplementing or approximating lookupWord. chapter-app.js is a single IIFE and exports only window.KW_roleFor and window.KW_colorizeGerman (grep-verified), so the real function is otherwise unreachable from a harness.

whyItFailed.observed: window.__P40 was created but every function reference was null; the harness reported "lookupWord not exported" for chapter-a1-8-goethemini1 and chapter-a1-15-cafe
whyItFailed.diagnosis: the injection point — the LAST occurrence of "})();" in chapter-app.js — is not inside the scope where lookupWord is declared. chapter-app.js contains multiple IIFEs (e.g. the loadGlobalLexicon block at :25), so the final "})();" closes a different function than the main module body.
whyItFailed.secondaryFailures: two later chapters returned "Failed to fetch" — the harness page also reset once mid-run, which is why an earlier attempt lost its in-memory results (per-chapter persistence was added afterwards).
whyItFailed.confidence: PROVEN that the export did not reach the intended scope; the exact correct injection point was NOT identified in this phase.

whatThisDoesNotChange: the P39 static findings stand: normWord() lowercases, so Deutsch/deutsch share one WORDIDX slot (chapter-app.js:2717, :2430)
a1-3 authors { de: "Zahl", plural: "Zahlen" }, so KW_INFLECTIONS maps lowercase "zahlen" to the NOUN lemma — Candidate 1 remains disproven for Zahlen
the 8 legitimate Zahlen noun uses all carry authored roles/types and resolve through the token path, so they remain insulated from any guess-path change
lookupWord already contains the expectedClass homograph guard at :2735-2738 — the machinery exists; what is unproven is its behaviour on these specific surfaces

conditionStatus.8_realImplementationUsed: FAILED — the real implementation could not be reached
conditionStatus.overall: condition 8 failed, so per the brief Candidate 2 is not recommended

letterA.reasoning: Candidate 2 cannot solve it — the popup side is already correct by design (ROLE_COLOR_VAR maps letter|name|conjunction to --ink-secondary, chapter-app.js:2022) and the defect is the SPAN, which comes from guessRole rule 6, a function this phase is forbidden to touch. It would require Candidate 4 (a narrow single-letter guard), which is a separate decision. It is 1 finding, cosmetically inconsistent, and the popup a learner sees is correct.
letterA.confidence: PROVEN for both colour sources (source-read in P38/P39)

nextStepToUnblock.single: identify the correct injection point inside chapter-app.js’s MAIN IIFE and re-run the same harness unchanged.
nextStepToUnblock.how: locate the module body’s own closing sequence rather than the file’s last "})();" — e.g. anchor on a string unique to the main body (the existing "window.KW_roleFor = roleFor;" assignment at :966 is inside that scope and is a safe, verified anchor to append exports next to).
nextStepToUnblock.cost: one edit to the harness, one run; no production change
nextStepToUnblock.note: until that runs, every statement about expectedClass behaviour remains reasoning, not measurement — the same standard applied in P22 (isolation disproved a sweep reading), P27/P29 (a full pass overturned an isolation verdict) and P34 (instrumentation overturned two prior hypotheses).
